boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Penn State rituals, ceremonies, and recurring campus practices.

cards.title: Answer the “We Are” call
cards.subtitle: A call-and-response heard across Penn State life
cards.notes: Listen for the call, then answer “Penn State”; the University documents its first Beaver Stadium use in 1976 and its lasting campus role.
cards.short_summary: A concise call-and-response that connects Penn Staters at games, ceremonies, and beyond.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State says cheerleaders first used “We Are Penn State” in Beaver Stadium in 1976, and the cheer became permanent by 1981.
cards.source_title: Why we say ‘We Are’ | Penn State University
cards.access_notes: The University describes the cheer as used at Beaver Stadium, freshman welcomes, graduations, and as a greeting.

cards.title: Guard the Lion Shrine
cards.subtitle: Homecoming at the Nittany Lion Shrine
cards.notes: During Homecoming, visit the shrine after the parade to see the Lion Ambassadors’ program centered on protecting the landmark.
cards.short_summary: A Homecoming vigil tied to the campus’s iconic limestone lion.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State states that Lion Ambassadors host Guard the Lion Shrine immediately after each Homecoming parade, based on protecting the statue from rival defacement.
cards.source_title: Student Programs | Penn State Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of Homecoming; consult the current Homecoming program for timing.

cards.entity_name: “For the Glory” Penn State Alma Mater
cards.title: Sing “For the Glory of Old State”
cards.subtitle: Penn State’s alma mater
cards.notes: Learn the opening line before a Penn State gathering, then join the communal singalong when it is performed.
cards.short_summary: A song tradition reaching back to Fred Lewis Pattee’s 1901 composition.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State identifies “For the Glory of Old State” as the alma mater’s opening line and says singing it has been a tradition since its 1901 composition.
cards.access_notes: The University presents the alma mater as a Penn State singalong tradition.

cards.title: Wear white for the White Out
cards.subtitle: Beaver Stadium football tradition
cards.notes: If attending a designated White Out, follow the event guidance and wear white so the stadium’s coordinated crowd effect can take shape.
cards.short_summary: A designated football-game tradition built around a stadium-wide field of white.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State lists the White Out as a signature football tradition in which a roughly 110,000-person crowd wears white.
cards.access_notes: Occurs for designated football games; game admission and current event details vary.

cards.entity_name: Blue Band Drum Major Forward Flip
cards.title: Watch the drum major’s forward flip
cards.subtitle: Penn State Blue Band pregame pageantry
cards.notes: Watch the Blue Band’s field entrance from a safe spectator location; the drum major’s running forward flip is part of the ritual.
cards.short_summary: A 1971-born Blue Band flourish that became a Penn State football fixture.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State documents that the drum major flip became a Penn State tradition after its 1971 debut and evolved into a running front flip.
cards.source_title: Head over heels for the Blue Band drum major | Penn State University
cards.access_notes: Observe during Blue Band appearances and follow venue staff directions.

cards.title: Learn THON’s hourly Line Dance
cards.subtitle: Penn State IFC/Panhellenic Dance Marathon
cards.notes: Follow the dancers’ lead during THON Weekend; a new routine is designed each year and returns throughout the event.
cards.short_summary: An annually refreshed, repeating dance that keeps THON Weekend moving.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State reports that THON’s Line Dance is performed hourly and that each THON Weekend receives a newly designed dance with unique moves and words.
cards.source_title: THON 2020: The Big Reveal | Penn State University
cards.access_notes: Takes place during THON Weekend; participation and spectator arrangements are event-specific.

cards.title: Follow the Homecoming Parade route
cards.subtitle: University Park and downtown State College
cards.notes: Check the current Homecoming schedule, then watch the parade as it travels through campus and downtown before the shrine program.
cards.short_summary: A long-running Homecoming procession joining students, alumni, and the town.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State says its community has observed Homecoming regularly since 1920 and identifies the parade as one of its oldest traditions.
cards.source_title: The history of Penn State Homecoming: Remembrance, reflection and revelry | Penn State University
cards.access_notes: Annual Homecoming scheduling and route details vary; use the current official program.

cards.title: Take the Lion Shrine photo twice
cards.subtitle: First day and graduation-day photo ritual
cards.notes: Photograph the shrine from the surrounding plaza on your first day, then revisit in cap and gown at graduation without climbing the sculpture.
cards.short_summary: A documented before-and-after photo ritual framing a Penn State degree.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State’s visitor guide describes a tradition of students photographing themselves on the Lion as freshmen and again in caps and gowns at graduation.
cards.access_notes: Use the surrounding public area and respect any posted monument-access guidance.

cards.title: Ring the thesis-completion gong
cards.subtitle: Schreyer Honors College thesis tradition
cards.notes: Schreyer Scholars who complete their thesis may ring the gong; visitors can spot it at the Medals Ceremony and in college displays.
cards.short_summary: A thesis milestone marked by one ceremonial gong strike.
cards.evidence_claim: Schreyer Honors College states that, since 2000, only Scholars who have completed their thesis may strike its gong.
cards.access_notes: Ringing is limited to Scholars who have completed their thesis; ceremony access varies.

cards.title: Look for the Old Willow successor
cards.subtitle: Old Main lawn
cards.notes: Pause by the Old Main lawn to see the current willow and learn how Penn State propagates successor trees to continue the campus lineage.
cards.short_summary: A living-campus tradition sustained through successor saplings.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn State describes planting an Old Willow sapling on the Old Main lawn as continuing a tradition that spans University history.
cards.source_title: Cultivating the next ‘Old Willow’ | Penn State University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landscape feature; access is subject to campus conditions and posted guidance.
